correctness.rationale: In finite commuting named permutation systems, the partition of (x,f_i(x),f_i^{-1}(x)) is C²-definable with two variables: equalities of any two images become two-edge atomic formulas with one bound y. Commutation makes this partition constant on every joint orbit. For any vertex x, its complete atomic two-type multiplicities among other vertices are determined by its partition, the partition histogram, and the all-false residual pairs. These data remain closed under the two-variable counting-quantifier induction, giving both implications of the exact histogram criterion. For two named bijections the exhibited Z/5 pair g=+2 versus g=+3 has equal collision profile but is not isomorphic (the centralizer of f=+1 consists of translations); a C³ formula detects g=f². Full labelled commuting-pair enumeration modulo simultaneous conjugation through n=6 gives isotype/profile counts (1/1,4/4,8/8,21/21,39/38,92/82), so n=5 is minimal. Finally, three variable symbols suffice to define the action of any fixed group word, identify a rooted permutation orbit via words of lengths at most n, and count orbit copies; commutativity is not required for this C³ upper bound. Independently reconstructed finite n≤5 census corroborates; the universal claims are deductive, not inferred from finite sampling.
residual_risks: Three-variable characteristic formulas are size-dependent and can be enormous; no uniform bounded-length sentence is claimed. Exhaustive small census does not replace C² and C³ proof.
